answers.answer: Shuffle all 4 III cards and place them face down at the bottom; shuffle all 9 II cards and deal 5 face down above them; shuffle all 3 I cards and deal 1 face down on top. Return unused I and II cards to the box unseen.
answers.evidence: Setup: “shuffle…deal”; return unused Conflict cards unseen.

answers.answer: Four-player human: score marker starts at 1; three-player: 0. Both start with 2 Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; 3 troops in the nearest garrison and 9 in supply; 1 water.

Yes, you may Reveal while Agents remain, and after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of Player Turns. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed then, not Agent-turn cards. At Clean Up all cards in front of you, from both Agent and Reveal turns, go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Player Turns; Reveal Turn.

answers.answer: No: the entry cost must be payable immediately before resolving destination or played-card effects, so Agent-box gains cannot pay it. One card sends one Agent using one matching icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Agent Turn; entry-cost timing.

answers.answer: You may deploy the 3 troops recruited this turn plus up to 2 from the garrison: at most 5 total in this example. At a non-Combat destination, you cannot deploy; recruited troops go to your garrison. Troops are recruited from your personal supply.

A Spy Agent icon grants access to any board space connected to an observation post where you currently have a Spy; it does not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to bypass another player’s Agent, never your own. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy to draw 1 card; choose immediately after placement and before space/card effects. The same Spy cannot pay both Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence; two different Spies may. Only one Gather Intelligence draw per placement.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spy Agent access, Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence.

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops = 4, one sandworm = 3, four revealed swords = 4. If your final unit is removed, strength becomes 0. You cannot play Combat Intrigue without at least one unit in the Conflict.

Yes. Passing is not binding if another player later plays; the window closes after all involved players pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to supply (not garrison), sandworms to the bank.

In both player counts, tied first players each get the second reward and nobody wins or takes the Conflict card. In four-player play, if exactly two tie first, the remaining players compete for third reward; in three-player play there are no other rewards. A zero-strength player receives none.

One or more sandworms double rewards once; multiple worms do not multiply further. Control and battle icons on won Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For a reward offering 3 spice to gain 1 VP, you may pay 3 spice once for 1 VP or pay 6 spice to take the doubled 2 VP.

After winning and taking a Conflict card face up into your supply, check it against another face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply. A matching pair must be flipped face down for 1 VP. During Endgame, a wild icon may match any one of the three icons in your supply.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat winner procedure; Battle Icons.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence gain 1 VP; lose that VP below 2 and regain it on reaching 2 again. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, retain it if dropping below 4, and earn it again on returning to 4; the first to 4 gains the Alliance token and its 1 VP. Tying the holder does not take it: a challenger must rise above. FAQ also says a holder losing Influence after a tie transfers it to a formerly tied player (or chooses among tied players); at 3 or lower, if no one has 4+, it returns to board and holder loses its VP.
answers.evidence: Scoring: Faction Influence; FAQ: Alliance loss.

answers.answer: Spend Persuasion before, between, or after Reveal effects. Pool Persuasion across sources to buy one card, or split one source across cards. The Imperium Row refills to five, and you may buy a replacement immediately if you can afford it. Acquired cards go face up to your discard pile.

At an unoccupied Maker space, add 1 spice to its bonus spot during Makers; visiting gains all bonus spice there. Deep Desert (3 water) offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, 2 sandworms; Hagga Basin (1 water) offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, 1 worm. Worms cannot be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery or Imperial Basin while Shield Wall remains; removing it allows any Conflict. Hooks are required only when specified by the effect and are retained, not spent. Worms are placed directly in your Conflict quadrant, never garrison.
answers.evidence: Phase 4: Makers; Sandworms; Board Space Guide.

answers.answer: At the end of a round, 10+ VP by any player or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then compare VP. Tiebreakers are spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, in that order.

CHOAM is optional and Shaddam is optional. Shuffle 20 standard contracts and reveal 2 face up; the other 18 are face down in the bank. Add 4 Intrigue and 4 Imperium cards. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are Rise of Ix compatibility only and stay boxed.

With CHOAM, take a public face-up contract and refill from the bank if possible; if public offers are exhausted, gain 2 Solari (even if Shaddam’s reserved contracts remain). Harvest completes by visiting a Maker space and gaining the pictured spice amount total from all sources that turn; Immediate completes upon taking it; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.

No; a space contract can only be completed on a future turn if acquired after you already placed your Agent there, because you must hold it when sending the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM: Completing contracts; FAQ: Contract completion.

answers.answer: One shared scoring Rival is the third competitor. It receives the Ornithopter Objective; deal the other two eligible Objectives randomly to humans. First Player is the human whose Objective shows the marker; Rival is immediately clockwise, so order is First Player → Rival → other human. Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Setup; Agent turns.

answers.answer: For an occupied destination, ignore it and reveal again. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try its specified empty post; if none, ignore placement; either way reveal another Hagal card and continue the Agent turn. Ignore normal space costs/effects, applying only Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns; Place Spy cards.

answers.answer: Shuffle Objectives after omitting cards whose 1–3P/4/6P marking does not match; distribute one eligible card face up to each player. Its First Player marker selects the first player. Shaddam may be used only with CHOAM.

Bank resources and sandworms are not limited: make any convenient substitution if they run out. If your personal troop supply is empty, you cannot recruit more until troops return there. Gains come from the bank and payments return to the bank.

The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. Round Start reveals a Conflict, resolves controlled-location defense, then each player draws 5. If Recall does not trigger Endgame, human Agents return to Leaders; First Player passes clockwise with 3–4 humans. In two-player, Rival Agents return to supply and First Player passes to the other human.

Yes, board-space effects, Agent-box effects, and Faction advancement may be resolved in any order. No, entry requirements and costs must be met before effects resolve, so the visit’s Influence cannot meet its own entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Agent Turn; Influence-requirement spaces.

answers.answer: An optional arrow cost/effect may be paid only once per turn, not twice (sandworm reward doubling is the exception). Most card/space effects are mandatory; “may,” optional arrow costs, and black-X trash are exceptions. Intrigue play still requires meeting its conditions and paying all its costs.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Arrows / paying costs; FAQ: Mandatory effects and costs.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post; if none are in supply, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. If placement specifies an Agent-icon type, the post must connect to a space with that icon or the placement is not legal.

No, Infiltrate cannot bypass your own Agent. A Spy does not give a free Agent turn: play a card and meet its normal access condition. No, two Spies cannot each provide Gather Intelligence on one placement; at most one draw is allowed.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Infiltrate; Gather Intelligence; Spy Agent access.

answers.answer: The controller gets its separate bonus whenever any player, including itself, visits: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. Winning the named Conflict places/replaces control. When a controlled Conflict is revealed, the controller may deploy 1 troop from supply directly to Conflict without visiting.

Tie for second: each tied player gets third reward; winner keeps first reward and card; no further rewards. Tie for third: tied players get nothing. Three tied first: each gets second reward, nobody takes the card, and no other rewards, in either three- or four-player play.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Combat ties; Three tied for first.

answers.answer: In a three-player Conflict with three distinct positive strengths, first and second get their rewards; third gets none. The same ordinary rank rule applies to two humans plus the Rival: first and second receive rewards, untied third does not.
answers.evidence: Phase 3: Resolve Combat; Player count determines ranks.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues: own Agent or Reveal turns; Combat Intrigues: Combat only and only with a unit in Conflict; Endgame Intrigues: at game end. Keep Intrigues face down, separate from deck; after resolving, face up in discard. If deck empties, shuffle its discard into a new deck.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Intrigue cards; FAQ: Draw timing.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard is a card of your choice from your hand, not an Intrigue unless specified. Secrets’ Steal Intrigue makes each opponent with 4+ Intrigues give one selected at random. The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon lets you trash one Intrigue of your choice from hand.

Trash effects can remove cards from hand, discard pile, or in play; ordinary cards return to the box and Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or instructed to trash itself. The Spice Must Flow acquire VP remains even if the card is later trashed.

Acquire-box effects resolve once when acquiring the card, not when playing it. If your deck is empty when drawing, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue. Unused Persuasion is lost at the end of Reveal and cannot carry forward.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed during Reveal stay in play face up until Clean Up (unless trashed). Two Fremen Bond cards can activate one another regardless of order, because each is the other’s “other” Fremen card. Clean Up moves them to discard.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: In play / Fremen Bond.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other board Agents, never the one just sent; it may act again on another Agent turn that round. Retreat moves a troop from Conflict to garrison. “Retreat any number” includes zero.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Recall Agent; Retreat; FAQ: Combat and troops.

answers.answer: A free-choice gain of two Influence must go to one chosen Faction; it cannot be split. A minimum-Influence effect requires that threshold; an Alliance icon requires holding that Faction’s Alliance token.

If holder loses Influence after being tied with two opponents, the former holder chooses which tied opponent receives the Alliance. If holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return it to the board; holder loses its Alliance VP.
answers.evidence: Scoring: Faction Influence; FAQ: Alliance loss.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used this turn. A card drawn after Reveal stays for next round, in addition to the five cards then drawn. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect stays face up until then, is used, then discarded.
No; after tying for first you did not win, so a “when you win” Intrigue cannot be played. If received as a reward for an outright win, it may be played immediately.
If VP and all four resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores can exceed the printed track’s 12.

No; all held contracts for the same space must be fulfilled with one Agent placement. A board-space contract is another Agent-turn effect and can resolve in any order with space and Agent-box effects, but must have been held when the Agent was sent.

Shaddam does not start with the two reserved Sardaukar contracts; only he may acquire them, choosing one instead of a generally available contract when acquiring. Set both aside before the initial shuffle: shuffle remaining 18, reveal 2 offers, leave 16 in bank, plus 2 reserved. His Signet deployment restriction takes effect immediately and lasts for that turn only.
answers.evidence: CHOAM: Setup changes; Reserved Sardaukar contracts; FAQ: Shaddam.

answers.answer: Feyd’s token starts on the leftmost Training track space and stays on the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica side begins face up. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.

Moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2. It can trigger again later if you first lose Influence and then regain it by moving up; moving down through 2 does not count. Moving Spacing Guild’s Favor from in play to discard at Clean Up does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding from hand does.

Accept Contract is Spice Trade, no cost, no Combat: always draw 1 card; without CHOAM contract icon gives 2 Solari, with CHOAM take/refill public contract or get 2 Solari if offers exhausted. It is non-Faction, no automatic Influence. Dutiful Service is Emperor, no cost, no Combat: gain 1 Emperor Influence plus the same contract-icon effect; the listed gain and automatic Faction advance are one Influence total, not two.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide; Faction status of contract spaces.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City, no cost, Combat yes; visitor recruits 1 troop and draws 1 card, controller gains 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw 1 card. Research Station: City, 2 water, Combat yes; recruit 2 troops and draw 2 cards.

Deep Desert costs 3 water, base choice 4 spice or (with Maker Hooks) 2 sandworms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water, base choice 2 spice or (with Hooks) 1 sandworm. Both also grant all bonus spice even when choosing worms. Hooks are not spent; effects specifying Hooks require having the token.

Both options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource cost. Option 1: take Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruit 1 troop, gain 1 water. Option 2: gain 1 water and optionally remove Shield Wall; it gives no troop.

High Council is Landsraad, no Combat, costs 5 Solari each visit. First visit puts your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and grants 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn thereafter. Later visits grant 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit 3 troops.

Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone gains one, then 6; each player may gain it only once. Take the third Agent, available this round and for the rest of the game. Rival obtaining Swordmaster also lowers the human cost to 6.

Imperial Privilege is Landsraad, costs 3 Solari, requires 2+ Emperor Influence, and is not Combat. You may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue; recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It gives no automatic Emperor Influence.
Shipping is Spice Trade, requires 2+ Guild Influence and costs 3 spice; it gives 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction. The free-choice Influence need not be Guild. It is not a Combat space.

Gather Support is Landsraad, non-Combat: choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari; recruit 2 troops, and if paying 2 also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery is City, Combat: choose 0 or 1 spice; gain 2 Solari free or 4 Solari if paying 1; controller separately gains 1 Solari.

Heighliner: Spacing Guild, costs 5 spice, gains 1 Guild Influence and recruits 5 troops; Combat yes. Desert Tactics: Fremen, costs 1 water, gains 1 Fremen Influence, recruits 1 troop, may trash a card; Combat yes. Sardaukar: Emperor, costs 4 spice, gains 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue and recruits 4 troops; Combat no.

Assembly Hall: Landsraad, no cost, non-Combat; draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during Reveal if your Agent is there. Espionage: Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice, non-Combat; gain 1 BG Influence, draw a card, place a Spy. Deliver Supplies: Spacing Guild, no cost, non-Combat; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.

False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent’s destination that turn; it can be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear’s red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ: False Orders; Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it remains unacquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.

Rival starts with 3 troops in garrison and remaining troops in supply, 2 Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside board, 3 Spies, 1 water, and score/Combat markers at 0. Shuffle House Hagal retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. Rival at 10+ VP triggers Endgame and can win.

As soon as its Solari, spice, Intrigue cards, and water total reaches printed Swordmaster value (each unit/card counts 1), spend exactly that amount in mandatory order: Solari, spice, Intrigue, water. Keep leftovers. Take its third Agent for immediate use this round.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Swordmaster resource total.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, spend 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP per set. Mixed totals do not qualify.

Choose the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by leftmost priority icon. Rival gains/losses VP at 2 Influence and gains/loses Alliance VP like a human, but does not receive 4-Influence track bonuses. A numbered Hagal Influence icon means that position in the Rival card’s Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: After Swordmaster; Agent turns.

answers.answer: No. With a two-destination card, choose only the destination matching current conditions (Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping; Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner); if it is occupied, reveal a new card without using the other destination.

Yes. At any Combat space deploy up to 2 available garrison troops even if the card recruited none; newly recruited troops deploy too. At a noncombat space recruited troops go to garrison. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus is simply omitted if unmet; it never blocks placement.

Unless specified, put a Spy at first available Faction post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing third/final supply Spy recalls the other two and triggers Scheme. Rival never recalls Spies for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: Scheme-recruited troops can deploy if the Rival visits a Combat space that same turn. A Place Spy card with no legal post is ignored, but Rival immediately reveals another Hagal card and continues because it has not placed an Agent.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: At Hagga/Deep Desert, Rival collects all bonus spice. With Hooks and a Conflict permitting worms, summon one at Hagga or two at Deep Desert instead of base spice; if it summons none, take base spice (2/4). Thus without Hooks, or at protected Conflict, take base spice.

At Combat start, if Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal one Hagal card and add its bottom swords; on Reshuffle reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then get their normal Combat Intrigue window. Unit-free Rival receives no bonus.

Yes: Rival gets control and defensive troop bonuses, battle-icon VP, and doubles rewards with worms; it wins cards normally. Always take optional Conflict VP if it can pay or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts: a contract reward gives 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
Total, announce and set strength during Reveal resolution, at any point; update as needed while resolving. If over 20, flip marker to +20 side and start again from the track beginning.
Leader’s Signet ability activates when Signet Ring is played to send an Agent on an Agent turn, not merely revealed. Cards may override normal game rules.
Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from a post to your supply, usually as a cost. It is not inherently Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those effects specify what the recall accomplishes.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spies & observation posts; Recall Spy icon.

answers.answer: The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand; an ordinary discard instruction discards from your hand and cannot discard Intrigue unless specified.

Doubling a one-Influence reward yields 2 Influence; because reward doubling permits the optional reward to be taken a second time, you may choose the same Faction or two different Factions. A single effect granting 2 Influence with free choice must put both in one Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling; Special Rules: Influence.

answers.answer: Resolve the Rival card’s printed Signet Ring ability. Do not substitute Scheme. It is triggered by the Hagal Signet Ring effect; no human Signet Ring card or Reveal turn is involved.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Rival Signet Ring and Scheme.

answers.answer: Maker Hooks effect takes one token if Rival lacks one; if it already has Hooks, take none. Wall removal works only if Rival has Hooks and Wall remains; without Hooks ignore it, and if Wall is already gone it has no effect.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Rival Hooks and Wall icons.

answers.answer: Secrets is Bene Gesserit, no cost, non-Combat; gain 1 BG Influence and draw an Intrigue from the deck. Each opponent with 4+ Intrigues also gives one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Secrets; Intrigue cards.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin is Spice Trade, no cost, Combat yes; visitor receives 1 base spice plus all bonus spice. Its controller separately gets 1 spice, so if visitor controls it that player gets both effects.
Reveal a new Conflict from top of deck and place it face up next to/on top of any unclaimed Conflict cards remaining from earlier rounds. Then resolve defensive bonus; after that each player draws 5.

Each player puts one cube at the bottom of each of four Influence tracks; Alliance tokens start on marked areas of those tracks, so nobody starts holding one. Shield Wall token is placed on the marked area below Spice Refinery.

First Player acts first, then clockwise; players continue taking one turn at a time. A Revealed player skips remaining turns; phase ends when all players Revealed. Combat Intrigue starts with First Player, proceeds clockwise; eligible players may play any number before passing.
Reveal Cards; Resolve Reveal Effects; Clean Up. Reveal effects may be resolved in any order.

Shuffle each human’s 10-card starter and place face down in supply. Omit CHOAM cards (including from both decks); shuffle Intrigue and Imperium decks separately face down; deal 5 face up to Imperium Row; place Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate stacks. Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies, Councilor, and all three Control markers start in personal supply.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 4 and 6; Human component layout.

answers.answer: Ordinarily buy any of five Imperium Row cards or Reserve Prepare the Way / The Spice Must Flow; cost appears at top right. These Persuasion purchases occur during Reveal turn.
Yes, ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional even with a legal placement/recall. Shield Wall removal is optional; once removed it is returned to box and cannot return later.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spies & observation posts; Shield Wall; FAQ: Mandatory effects.

answers.answer: The Agent icon on played card must match the destination’s upper-left icon. A connected Spy does not let a card with only City icon access Shipping. If card has the Spy Agent icon and a Spy at a connected post, it can access Shipping without recalling that Spy.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Agent Turn; Special Rules: Separate Spy costs and Spy Agent access.

answers.answer: Yes. On an Agent turn you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue; resources it grants before placement can pay the entry cost. Gains only after placing Agent, from destination or Agent card, cannot pay that entry cost.
answers.evidence: Phase 2: Player Turns, Plot Intrigue timing; Agent Turn.

answers.answer: No. Even after both humans Reveal, continue the Rival’s Agent turns while it has Agents in supply; proceed to Combat only after both humans Revealed and Rival used all Agents. Rival never Reveals.

| Accept Contract | Spice Trade | No |

| Deliver Supplies | Spacing Guild | No |

When its Conflict is revealed, controller may deploy 1 troop from supply directly to Conflict; it is optional and requires no visit. After rewards, all troops return to supply and all Combat markers reset to 0 before Makers.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: Round Start; Phase 3: Resolve Combat.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you; send one Agent from your Leader to a matching unoccupied space (subject to Spy rules); resolve its Agent box, not Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or discard pile, nor move an Agent already on the board as the placement.
Restriction applies immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send the Agent; he cannot defer it by ordering board-space effects first, and recruited troop cannot deploy that turn.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Shaddam; CHOAM: Shaddam’s Signet benefits.

answers.answer: With four different positive strengths and no worms, first gets first reward and takes card, second gets second reward, third gets third reward, fourth gets none. Winner takes card face up, then checks mandatory battle-icon match.
Players may choose Leaders or select randomly.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 3: “choose, or select at random.”

answers.answer: Draw from your own deck; if it is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue. You may not choose directly from discard pile.
Shuffle House Hagal and place deck near shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card.
All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. Later acquired token moves from bank onto that player’s garrison.
Yes, adjust the Combat marker when the Combat Intrigue resolves during the Combat Intrigue window. The Reveal-turn total is not fixed; use adjusted strength shown on track to resolve rewards.
Gained Solari, spice, or water come from the bank, not another player’s supply; payments return to bank.
Shuffle the 20 standard contract tokens face down, then flip 2 face up as offers and put the remaining 18 face down in bank. Offers and bank order are randomized; players do not choose/preset them.

Set aside both Sardaukar contracts before the contract shuffle; only Shaddam may acquire them, and he does not start with them. Shuffle the remaining 18, reveal 2 face-up public offers, and put 16 face down in bank, with 2 reserved Sardaukar contracts set aside.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: Setup changes; Reserved Sardaukar contracts.
